findings.description: Successful reprobe obtains a provider handle, swaps it under rdbg_smem_state_lock, then puts the prior reference under the same lock. This keeps exactly one reference reachable per output slot across repeated successful rebinds; module exit puts the current reference once.

qcom_smem_state_get writes smem_bit and rdbg_probe publishes smem_state while holding rdbg_smem_state_lock. send_interrupt_to_subsystem reads both fields and calls qcom_smem_state_update_bits under that lock, so the paired state cannot be observed mid-publication.
An error return from qcom_smem_state_get no longer overwrites the stored pointer with an ERR_PTR; the probe returns the lookup error.

residuals: There is still no per-device platform remove callback. The SMEM handle is retained as module-owned state until module exit to match the module-wide character-device lifetime; runtime behavior during device/provider unbind was not exercised.
Input IRQ identifier and already-open file behavior across platform unbind/rebind remain unverified.
No phone test, module load, unbind/rebind test, or host harness was run because adb devices -l showed no connected device.
